abstract: Stem cell spheroid-hydrogel platforms offer promise for bone defect repair, but implantation-associated oxidative stress, poor vascular ingrowth, and insufficient osteogenic cues limit their clinical translation. Here, we developed dual-NICHE (dual niche-instructive construct for bone healing and engraftment), a gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel containing human adipose-derived stem cell spheroids with spatially distinct intra-/perispheroidal niches. Within a single construct, these two niches provide complementary functions to simultaneously address the key bottlenecks in bone regeneration. The intraspheroidal niche incorporated bone morphogenetic protein-2-immobilized fibers to promote osteogenic differentiation, whereas the perispheroidal matrix contained Sr2+-tannic acid nanoparticles (NPs). Upon implantation, the NPs mitigated oxidative stress and supported vascular infiltration. Concurrently, the osteogenic cue promoted differentiation, while the NPs facilitated mineral nucleation and growth, as further supported by molecular dynamics simulations. Together, this spatial integration enhanced vascularized bone formation with a bone volume fraction of ∼13.5% using only 5208 cells per defect in a mouse calvarial model, providing a potentially translatable framework for bone regeneration.
